base:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create one high-fidelity AAA desktop game Practice setup screenshot for Legend of the Five Rings: Emperor Edition. Landscape 16:9, crisp readable English UI, polished final-game presentation.
Reference inputs: Image 1 is the approved game frame/material/typography style reference only; Image 2 is the approved navy/gold backdrop and lacquer craftsmanship reference only. Do not reproduce their page content. Make a new PRACTICE SETUP screen.
Design system: rich worn BLACK lacquer surfaces, restrained warm aged gold metal trim with small Japanese ornamental corner joins, ivory text, restrained pale teal readiness accents. Black panels distinctly contrast with the deep navy cloth backdrop. WeatheredQuill-like uppercase brush lettering for main and section headings only, tightly set but clearly readable; Caudex serif regular for body/controls and bold for deck names, generous line spacing. Keep all actual controls front-on, legible, large click targets, sober refined craftsmanship. No generic web dashboard, plain green boxes, sci-fi effects, gratuitous crests, enormous VS graphic, ornamental sidebars, tiny text, or overdecorated gutters. One gold primary action, secondary buttons black lacquer with gold edges. No live battle HUD, phase bar, hand, or match underway.
Product behavior portrayed: local Practice against the existing practice opponent, choose YOUR deck and the OPPONENT deck from saved decks or built-in presets. Show identity, Stronghold, Dynasty count, Fate count and a text readiness status. Existing Lion/Crane presets stay available. No multiplayer lobby, difficulty selection, first-player chooser, arbitrary rules toggles, coins, rewards, or new game mechanics. Stronghold thumbnails show believable original L5R card-format art, not invented giant card rules. Deck counts exclude starting cards. Any illustrated deck names/compositions are illustrative UI fixtures, not claims of authoritative legality. Small unobtrusive footer "Concept • illustrative deck selections".
Text must be spelled correctly. All panels fit comfortably within the screen with clear margins and spacing.

Variant A — balanced paired deck selection. One complete screenshot, no montage or inset.
Top header: small "Back" control left, "PRACTICE SETUP" heading, small game name right.
A concise subtitle "Choose your deck and your practice opponent."
Use two equally sized beautifully crafted wide black lacquer deck panels side by side, filling the central 70% of the composition. LEFT header "YOUR DECK", RIGHT header "OPPONENT'S DECK". Each has a modest authentic round clan medallion next to title (crane left, lion right), a large horizontal atmospheric Stronghold artwork crop in a thin gold frame, deck identity beneath, and enough breathable space.
LEFT: deck name "Crane — Court & Steel"; source "Saved deck"; Stronghold "Shinden Asahina"; numeric row "Dynasty 40" and "Fate 40"; check and "Ready to play"; two controls "Change deck" and "Edit deck".
RIGHT: deck name "Lion — Starter"; source "Built-in preset"; Stronghold "Halls of Memory"; numeric row "Dynasty 40" and "Fate 40"; check and "Ready to play"; one control "Change deck".
Small text row below panels: "Opponent: Practice AI". Bottom-right large glowing-but-subtle gold button "START PRACTICE" with small elegant arrow. Bottom-left quiet textlink "Open deck builder".
The design should make both sides equally understandable at a glance, with the gold start button clearly the next action. Use a calm deep navy backdrop with very faint gold mountain filigree, no room illustration needed. Header, panel border and buttons should look like they came from the approved game.

Variant B — library-first setup with persistent match summary. One complete screenshot, no montage or inset.
Top header: "Back", "PRACTICE SETUP", small game name.
LEFT 62% of usable width a deck library on black lacquer. Section title "CHOOSE YOUR DECK"; search field "Search decks…"; tabs "Saved decks" selected and "Presets". Below four large roomy horizontal rows, each showing a meaningful 100px Stronghold artwork thumbnail, deck name, clan/Stronghold text, Dynasty/Fate counts and status. Names never truncated.
First row selected with thin warm gold border and very subtle illumination: "Crane — Court & Steel", "Shinden Asahina", "Dynasty 40 · Fate 40", teal check "Ready to play".
Second: "Lion — Starter", "Halls of Memory", "Dynasty 40 · Fate 40", "Ready to play".
Third: "Crane — Court Draft", "Shinden Asahina", "Dynasty 36 · Fate 40", amber small warning "4 Dynasty cards needed".
Fourth: "Crane — Experiment", "Shinden Asahina", "Dynasty 40 · Fate 40", amber small warning "2 cards not implemented".
Bottom of this library quiet controls "Import deck" and "Deck builder".
RIGHT 34% a fixed black lacquer match summary, with comfortable spacing. Title "YOUR MATCH". Two stacked slots; first subtly gold-highlighted "YOUR DECK", named "Crane — Court & Steel", small round crane medallion, "Ready to play". Second "OPPONENT'S DECK", "Lion — Starter", "Practice AI", small lion medallion, "Change deck". Thin gold divider between slots.
Bottom of right panel a concise line "Both decks are ready." then large gold "START PRACTICE" button. A secondary "Edit selected deck" text button above start. No extra explicit Select confirmation: highlight selection is already applied to the active slot. Large text, very few visible deck rows, meaningful card art, high clarity.

Variant C — immersive focused setup overlay with inline draft feedback. One complete screenshot, no montage or inset.
Behind the UI is a softly defocused and dimmed view of the approved Japanese fortress war room: spacious wood hall, amber lantern light, central navy and gold playing table with no cards, dark timber columns, distant gold folding map screen. Background is peripheral atmosphere only, UI remains bright and legible. No people, weapons, piles of boxes, or foreground chairs.
A centered, wide black lacquer setup panel about 78% of screen width and 82% of screen height, fine gold frame and small sculpted corners. Header "PRACTICE SETUP" with close X top right.
Use two wide horizontal deck slots stacked, big stronghold thumbnails at left, text in middle and "Change deck" on right, no sidebars. Top slot heading "YOUR DECK", name "Crane — Court Draft", subline "Shinden Asahina", count row "Dynasty 36 · Fate 40". Bottom slot heading "OPPONENT'S DECK", name "Lion — Starter", subline "Halls of Memory · Practice AI", count row "Dynasty 40 · Fate 40", subtle check "Ready to play". Clan medallions small and tasteful.
Directly UNDER the YOUR DECK slot, inside its boundaries, one elegant inset black lacquer feedback strip with thin muted amber edge: a small amber exclamation icon, bold "4 Dynasty cards needed", supporting text "Your draft is saved. Add 4 Dynasty cards to begin.", and a very clear secondary control "Edit deck". This is the only readiness error, no popup, no repeated alert text.
Bottom: quiet "Back" button left; "START PRACTICE" button right visibly disabled, muted engraved brass lettering on black lacquer with gold edge, no bright primary gold fill until both decks are ready. Helper immediately above it "Finish your deck to begin."
A calm useful draft-blocked state with a single clear correction, rendered as an atmospheric AAA game setup overlay.
